request.spec:
The screen gains a header with counters, shown at all times: the number of people on the sheet
(retired people included), the number of claims in each status (DRAFT, OPEN, PENDING, SETTLED,
VOID), the sheet's due-total and the sheet's overdue-total. Each counter always equals the figure
it repeats: the status counts those of the summary, the two totals the sheet's totals.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The screen gains a header with counters, shown at all times: the number of people on the sheet
(retired people included), the number of claims in each status (DRAFT, OPEN, PENDING, SETTLED,
VOID), the sheet's due-total and the sheet's overdue-total. Each counter always equals the figure
it repeats: the status counts those of the summary, the two totals the sheet's totals.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header counters are in, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**What changed:**
- **New component** `features/header/header.ts` shows the people count, one claim count per status (DRAFT, OPEN, PENDING, SETTLED, VOID), the due-total and the overdue-total, using the test's `data-testid`s (`header-people-count`, `header-claims-<STATUS>-count`, `header-due-total`, `header-overdue-total`).
- **`features/people/people.ts`** puts the header at the top of the sheet. It takes its numbers from the same values the summary and totals already use, so they can't disagree:
  - The status counts come from the summary's per-status counts.
  - The due-total and overdue-total come from the sheet totals (`rollup-due-total`, `rollup-overdue-total`).
  - The people count is the full list of people on the sheet, so retired people are counted even when "show retired" is off.

The server and stored data didn't need to change, since every figure was already worked out on the front end.

The header only appears once a sheet is loaded, because all the figures belong to a sheet. Before that there is nothing to count.
